2.2a — Spikes: Collisions, Health & Death

In lesson 2.1a you built coins that you pass through. Today you build spikes that you bump into. By asking two simple questions — how is this similar to the coin, and how is it different? — you unlock the second half of Unity's 2D physics engine: solid collisions, health tracking, and the death loop.

Comparative Thinking ~15 min

Computer scientists do not reinvent the wheel for every new feature. Whenever you encounter a new game mechanic, compare it to a problem you have already solved. Compare the Coin you built yesterday with the Spike you are building today:

FeatureCoin Pickup (Lesson 2.1a)Hazardous Spike (Today)
Physics TypeTrigger (Is Trigger = true). Intangible; player walks through.Solid Collision (Is Trigger = false). Physical wall; player bumps and stops.
Unity MessageOnTriggerEnter2D(Collider2D other)OnCollisionEnter2D(Collision2D collision)
Parameter ReceivedCollider2D other (just the component touched).Collision2D collision (holds contact points, relative velocity, and collider).
Tag Checkother.CompareTag("Coin")collision.gameObject.CompareTag("Spikes")
Stat AffectedIncreases wealth: ChangeCoins(+1)Decreases health: ChangeHealth(-1)
Object LifecycleConsumed on touch: Destroy(other.gameObject)Persists forever: remains dangerous in the world.

Socratic: Similarities & Differences

  1. How is the spike similar to the coin? Name at least two things both mechanics share in their logic flow.
  2. How is the spike different from the coin? Why would a game feel completely broken if spikes had Is Trigger = true and destroyed themselves on touch like coins?
  3. In OnCollisionEnter2D, why do we write collision.gameObject.CompareTag("Spikes") instead of collision.CompareTag(...)? (Look closely at the parameter type: is Collision2D a GameObject, a Collider, or a data container?)
Build Lab ~20 min

Step 1 — Verify the Spike Collider. In Assets/Prefabs/Spikes:

  1. Verify it has a BoxCollider2D.
  2. Ensure Is Trigger is unchecked (spikes are solid obstacles!).
  3. Ensure its Tag is set to Spikes.

Step 2 — Add Health and Death to StatManager.cs. Open Assets/Scripts/StatManager.cs and expand it with health tracking:

    [SerializeField] private int health = 3;

    public void ChangeHealth(int amount)
    {
        health += amount;
        Debug.Log("Health Changed! New Health: " + health);

        if (health <= 0)
        {
            Debug.Log("Player Died!");
            HandleDeath();
        }
    }

    private void HandleDeath()
    {
        // Halve coins rounded down as a death penalty
        coins = Mathf.FloorToInt(coins / 2f);
        health = 3;
        UnityEngine.SceneManagement.SceneManager.LoadScene("Start");
    }

Step 3 — Add OnCollisionEnter2D to PlayerController.cs. Open PlayerController.cs and add the collision handler right below OnTriggerEnter2D:

private void OnCollisionEnter2D(Collision2D collision)
{
    if (collision.gameObject.CompareTag("Spikes"))
    {
        if (StatManager.manager != null)
        {
            StatManager.manager.ChangeHealth(-1);
        }
    }
}

Save your files and hit Play in Unity. Walk into a spike! Your player physically stops against the spike, and the Console logs Health Changed! New Health: 2. Hit it three times: health hits 0, your coins are halved, and the Start scene loads!

Bug Hunt: Collision vs. Trigger Bugs

  1. If you accidentally check Is Trigger on the Spikes prefab, what happens when the player touches them? Does OnCollisionEnter2D ever fire?
  2. What happens if you delete if (health <= 0) from ChangeHealth? What would health do if you kept bumping spikes indefinitely?
  3. Why does HandleDeath() use Mathf.FloorToInt(coins / 2f) instead of regular integer division? What would happen if a player had 1 coin when they died?
Tinker ~15 min

Tinker: Exploring Collision Data

  1. In OnCollisionEnter2D, add Debug.Log("Impact velocity: " + collision.relativeVelocity);. Bump into a spike at different angles. What information does Collision2D give you that Collider2D could not?
  2. How could a game use collision.relativeVelocity.magnitude to create fall damage (only take damage if moving faster than 10 units/sec)?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Articulate how spikes are similar to coins and how they are different
  • Explain the difference between OnTriggerEnter2D and OnCollisionEnter2D
  • Explain why spikes use solid colliders (Is Trigger = false)
  • Trace the execution of ChangeHealth(-1) through death and scene reload
  • Commit your working spike hazard system to GitHub
